question:
I am trying to materialise a DBT metric using the following code and am getting an error.

My metric is pretty normal except I am trying to leverage the "non time based metrics" features described in this github issue : https://github.com/dbt-labs/dbt_metrics/issues/97

metric:

select *
from {{ metrics.calculate(
    metric_list=[
        metric('median_list_price')
    ],
    grain='all_time',
    dimensions=['product_code'],
) }}

Error:

column calendar.date_all_time does not exist

Versions:

  • dbt-core: 1.4.5
  • dbt-labs/metrics: 1.4.0

I cannot find any good solutions when googling for this specific error but I came across the solution in the DBT slack channel so cross posting here.

To make the question more self contained here is the metric definition that is referenced in the metrics.calculate call

metric definition

version: 2

metrics:
  - name: median_list_price
    label: TODO
    model: ref('list_price_analysis')
    calculation_method: median
    expression: charge_rate
    timestamp: created_date
    time_grains: [all_time]
    dimensions:
      - product_code
title: DBT metrics.calculate error: calendar.date_all_time does not exist
answer:
Remove the grain='all_time' and the error goes away.

As of dbt-metrics 1.4.x you can omit the time_grain when calling metrics.calculate and the default behaviour is to compute the aggregate accross the entire dataset. So the corrected call to metrics.calculate is (not grain key is removed)

select *
from {{ metrics.calculate(
    metric_list=[
        metric('median_list_price')
    ],
    dimensions=['product_code'],
) }}
